paras: The killing of Mrs. John Gundy took place in Amarillo, Texas, in 1903, when the house of John Gundy, a Black property owner who had been ordered to leave the town, was fired into and his wife was killed. The case is known only from a one-sentence news brief, which did not name the attackers or report any arrest.

According to the brief, Gundy, described as "a negro," had been "ordered out of Amarillo" but "owned property" there and "refused to go." The report does not say who gave the order, when it was given, or what reason, if any, was offered for it.

After Gundy's refusal, unidentified persons fired into his house, and his wife was killed. The brief gives no date for the shooting, no number of attackers, and no name for the woman; it does not report that Gundy himself was hurt.
No report of an inquest, arrest or prosecution appears in the coverage, and it does not show whether Gundy stayed in Amarillo.

The only account found ran on August 29, 1903, on the front page of the Scranton Chronicle, a weekly in Scranton, Mississippi, under the headline "He Refused to Leave." The item was a single sentence of the kind carried in miscellany columns, without a dateline, source or comment, and its headline put the weight on Gundy's refusal rather than on the killing. No Texas report, wire original or Black-press account of the shooting was found.

reader.title: Killing of Mrs. John Gundy
bases: The only report describes a Black property owner 'ordered out of Amarillo' who refused to go, after which his house was fired into and his wife killed; the killing was the enforcement of an order to leave, by attackers the report does not identify (A2).

A2 reports a woman killed when her house was fired into, plainly without lawful authority, and links it to her husband's refusal to obey an order to leave town (a racial-offense pretext); but it names no shooters and gives no number, so whether a group of three or more acted is not shown, and the one-sentence brief is the only report found.
Only one report was found, a one-sentence brief in a Mississippi weekly (A2); no Texas paper, wire original or Black-press account turned up.

record_check.dossier: Only the wife (unnamed) was killed; Gundy's house was fired into but no injury to him is reported. Listing both is acceptable only if Gundy is understood as the target, not a casualty.
